description: Solo team by Rozeena (rose00645121) building TerraDetective AI for the 'Be An Earth System Trend Detective!' challenge — detecting Earth system trends with NASA POWER / MERRA-2 data.
summary: TerraDetective AI turns 40+ years of NASA POWER climate data into a local, checkable story. Pick any place on Earth — by map click or search — and the app measures its warming rate with a 95% confidence interval, flags anomaly years, counts dangerous-heat days, and reveals which present-day city its 2050 climate will resemble.
details: Climate change stays abstract until you can see it in your own city. TerraDetective AI makes it personal and verifiable: choose any location on Earth and the app queries NASA's POWER API (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources, NASA Langley Research Center) live for 40+ years of temperature and precipitation data for those exact coordinates — free, no API key, no pre-baked datasets. A statistical 'trend detective' pipeline then investigates the record. It estimates the warming or cooling rate in °C per decade by least squares, with a 95% confidence interval, p-value and R², scans for anomaly years beyond ±2σ, and counts days per year above 35 °C from daily data, decade by decade. Three signature features present the evidence: Was This Normal? gives any month a verdict (NORMAL / UNUSUAL / NOT NORMAL) with z-score, percentile and '1-in-N-year' rarity against its own 40-year baseline; Future Twin City extrapolates the measured trend to 2050 and reveals which present-day city's climate the place will feel like; and an AI detective narrative (heuristic by default, upgradeable to a free-tier LLM, always labeled with its provider) writes the case up in plain language. Every investigation gets a shareable URL and a downloadable Markdown case file. If NASA is unreachable, the API returns an honest error — it never invents numbers. Four more investigations round out the case (all deterministic, all from the same NASA record): Season Shift Detective compares the first 10 years of the record against the last 10 — has the hottest month moved? the wettest month? how much has the place's own 'summer core' (its three consecutive warmest months, so southern-hemisphere seasons work too) warmed? Compare Two Places runs the same investigation on two locations side by side — warming rate with confidence interval, anomaly count, season shift and danger-days change. The map offers a NASA GIBS satellite layer (MODIS Terra true-color imagery) alongside the default base map, so detectives can look at the real Earth from space while they pick a case. And the detective narrative speaks two languages: the heuristic report is available in English or Roman Urdu — hand-written templates carrying exactly the same statistics — because climate evidence should reach the people who live it, in the language they read.
